info.title: isuzu-unity-cli - drive a running Unity Editor from the terminal
info.description: Drive a running Unity Editor from the terminal: read the console, compile, run tests, browse and edit the scene, capture the Game and Scene views. Pairs with the jp.shiranui-isuzu.unity-mcp Unity package, which the Editor serves MCP from directly.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Show what is installed, where, and what is stale

commands.name: jobs
commands.description: List background jobs, show one, or wait for one to end

commands.name: mcp-stdio
commands.description: Bridge stdio to the Editor's MCP endpoint (for MCP clients)

commands.name: projects
commands.description: List Editors that are currently running

commands.name: setup
commands.description: Register with an MCP client and install the skill

commands.name: tools
commands.description:
List tools, or print one tool's full schema as JSON
With a name the output is the same with or without --raw

commands.name: uninstall
commands.description: Remove everything this tool put on the machine

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Bring the CLI and every project's package to the newest

commands.name: upgrade

commands.name: verify
commands.description:
Recompile, optionally run the tests, read the console,
and answer with one exit code

options.name: --project
options.description:
Which Editor to use; needed when several are running.
Either the product name or the project folder the
window title shows; a unique part of either will do
Only this project's package; otherwise every Editor that
is running

options.name: --raw
options.description:
Print the JSON summary instead of the short report
Exit codes: 0 verified, 1 compile or tests failed, 2 an option is wrong, 3 no
Editor or an ambiguous one, 4 timed out. Console errors are reported but never
fail the run, because entries from earlier in the session linger.
JOBS OPTIONS

options.name: --compact
options.description:
Print JSON without indentation. Already the default when
output is piped or redirected, which is how an agent
reads it; this forces it in a terminal too

options.name: --version
options.description: Show the version

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
TOOLS AND MCP-STDIO OPTIONS

options.name: --group
options.description:
Only these groups: diagnostics, authoring, rendering,
timeline, build, code, input. On mcp-stdio it narrows
what the client is offered, which it otherwise pays for
on every request: every tool together is about 43,000 tokens
and diagnostics alone is about 11,000
VERIFY OPTIONS

options.name: --no-compile
options.description: Skip the compile step

options.name: --test
options.description: Also run a test suite

options.name: --test-mode
options.description: Which suite; defaults to edit

options.name: --assembly
options.description: Restrict the run to one test assembly

options.name: --filter
options.description: Restrict the run to matching test names

options.name: --category
options.description: Restrict the run to one NUnit category

options.name: --timeout
options.description:
Give up after this long; defaults to 300
Give up waiting after this long; defaults to 300. The job
itself keeps running in the Editor
Exit codes: 0 the job completed, 1 it failed or was cancelled, 2 an option is wrong,
3 no Editor or an ambiguous one, 4 the wait timed out.
ENVIRONMENT
UNITY_MCP_STATE_DIR            Where the Editor writes its descriptors, when that is
not a path this process would find on its own. Several
may be given, separated the way PATH is. From WSL2 the
Windows Editor writes to
/mnt/c/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/UnityMCP
UNITY_MCP_HOST                 Replaces 127.0.0.1 in the descriptor's endpoint. The
Editor binds loopback only, so this reaches it only
with a port proxy or mirrored networking in front of
it; it is an escape hatch, not the usual setup.
UNITY_MCP_TRACE                Any non-empty value prints stage timings on stderr,
measured from the process start time the OS recorded.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR              Claude Code's configuration directory, in place of
~/.claude. setup, doctor and uninstall take both the
skills directory and .claude.json from it.
CODEX_HOME                     Codex's configuration directory, in place of ~/.codex,
holding config.toml and the skills directory.
SETUP OPTIONS

options.name: --logs
options.description: How many console errors to report; defaults to 20

options.name: --wait
options.description:
Poll until the job ends and print only its last answer.
Needs an id. What holds the Editor up is reported on
stderr while the wait lasts

options.name: --agent
options.description:
Which agents to set up: claude-code, claude-desktop,
codex, cursor, gemini, vscode. Defaults to every one
found installed.

options.name: --client
options.description:
Another spelling of --agent. If both are given, --agent
is the one that counts.

options.name: --mcp
--scope
options.description:
Where the Claude Code entry goes. "project" writes
.mcp.json in the Unity project and reads the token from
$UNITY_MCP_TOKEN, so no token is committed.

options.name: --no-skill
options.description:
Do not install the skill
DOCTOR OPTIONS

options.name: --fix
options.description:
Reinstall stale skills and rewrite stale MCP entries
UPDATE OPTIONS

options.name: --release
options.description:
Go to this release instead of the newest
Install this release instead of the newest, e.g. v4.1.1.
The way back when a new one turns out to be broken.
UNINSTALL OPTIONS

options.name: --dry-run
options.description:
Say what would change and change nothing
Four of the six ways the package can be installed cannot be updated from here - a
working copy, a folder under Packages/, and anything VCC or ALCOM manages. Those are
named with the step that does move them.
UPGRADE OPTIONS

options.name: --yes
options.description: Actually remove, rather than listing what would be removed

options.name: --json
options.description:
Arguments as one JSON object
--<name> <value>               Individual argument. Naming one twice sends a list, which
